External links for this lesson. All checked to load from this environment as of the date this
page was written. (As with the previous foundation lesson: eCFR's own rendered pages block
automated/proxied traffic here even though a human browser reaches them fine, so the CFR link
below is a verified-loading mirror of the same official text rather than the eCFR page itself.
The regulation text quoted in this lesson comes straight from eCFR's public API regardless.)

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 606.171, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — Cornell Law School's Legal Information Institute mirrors the current CFR, including the
  biological product deviation reporting section (BPDR) quoted in this lesson. Use this to check
  whether the reporting trigger or the 45-day deadline has changed since this lesson was written;
  the dated snapshot in this repo's `sources/` folder won't update automatically.

- **[ICH Q9(R1): Quality Risk Management](https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/ICH_Q9(R1)_Guideline_Step4_2023_0126.pdf)**
  — the actual current guideline this lesson's risk-ranking vocabulary is built on, published by
  the International Council for Harmonisation. Read the risk assessment section (Section 5,
  "Risk Assessment") if you want the source-level definitions of hazard, harm, and risk behind
  likelihood/severity/detectability — this is guidance-tier methodology, not an FDA regulation,
  which is exactly the distinction this lesson's Q1 checks for.

- **[NIST CSRC Glossary: residual risk](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/residual_risk)**
  — NIST's Computer Security Resource Center glossary entry for residual risk, useful as a
  plain, non-GxP-specific definition to cross-check the inherent-vs-residual distinction in this
  lesson against the same vocabulary as it's used in security/GRC contexts. Track 4 of this
  curriculum (`grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`) will lean on this same NIST vocabulary
  directly.

- **[Preventive, Detective & Corrective controls | Administrative, Physical & Technical measures](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9iT-PwvhNWs)**
  (Security For You, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. Teaches the
  preventive/detective/corrective taxonomy in a general IT/physical-security context, not a
  blood-establishment one; use it to hear the same three-way vocabulary applied to firewalls and
  badge readers instead of platelet units, which is a good test of whether the vocabulary actually
  stuck independent of this lesson's scenario. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on
  2026-11-11.

- **[iSixSigma: FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis)](https://www.isixsigma.com/tools-templates/fmea/)**
  — an industry-practice overview of FMEA and the risk priority number (RPN) calculation this
  lesson's worked numeric example borrows from. Useful if you want the fuller engineering-side
  version of the likelihood/severity/detectability math before adapting it for a quality council
  packet — remember ICH Q9 itself doesn't mandate this specific formula or scale; this is an
  industry-practice source behind the illustrative method, not a regulatory or AABB citation.

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about risk and controls vocabulary.

- **[CISSP Domain 1: Security & Risk Management](https://destcert.com/resources/domain-1-security-and-risk-management/)**
  (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP training company) — a free written overview of
  Domain 1 that defines threat, vulnerability and risk and expresses risk as likelihood times
  impact. A good bridge from this lesson's vocabulary to how security certification study frames
  it. Supports CISSP Domain 1 (Security and Risk Management). Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Risk Management Concepts for CISSP: Threats, Vulnerabilities & Risk Analysis Explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yRO7QGCKQnE)**
  (CyberSec Academy) — a video walk-through of how threats and vulnerabilities combine into risk.
  A community-made study video, so treat it as a study aid and check it against the lesson.
  Supports CISSP Domain 1. Verified via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[CISSP Domain 1: Risk Assessment & the ALE Formula](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kEYgBZDhbpc)**
  (DD214 HQ, a small independent channel) — shows how likelihood and impact can be turned into a dollar figure (annualized
  loss expectancy), a quantitative contrast to this lesson's ranked-score example. Supports
  CISSP Domain 1. Verified via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Security Controls — CompTIA Security+ SY0-701](https://www.professormesser.com/security-plus/sy0-701/sy0-701-video/security-controls-sy0-701/)**
  (Professor Messer) — free, short video lesson on control categories and types (preventive,
  detective, corrective and others). Reinforces this lesson's controls taxonomy with a second
  teacher. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC Glossary: security control](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/security_control)**
  (NIST) — the standard glossary definition of a security control, with the sources it is drawn
  from. Handy for checking vocabulary precision. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).
